Configuration and settings

TL;DR

The Configuration view under the space manages Claude Code’s own configuration per project or user: hooks, commands, skills, agents, MCP servers, permissions, plugins. The commands and settings Tandem itself adds are listed below.

The Configuration tree

Below the space in the Tandem container, the Configuration view manages Claude Code configuration per scope (project or user): hooks, commands, skills, agents, MCP servers, permissions, and installed plugins — with add / open / delete from the tree and its context menus. The view follows your active project.

Choosing the repository

Tandem never assumes which folder of a multi-root workspace you mean. The active repository is chosen once and remembered per workspace:

  • the status-bar item Tandem: <product> / <repo>;

  • the <repo> ▾ button in the map;

  • Tandem: Switch Repository in the command palette.

Each repository has its own session and its own spaces in the store.

Commands

The commands the extension contributes, as the command palette lists them:

Command What it does

Tandem: Open Thinking Space

Pick a repository, then one of its thinking spaces; it opens in an editor tab.

Tandem: New Thinking Space

Create a thinking space for the active repository.

Tandem: Delete Thinking Space

Remove one.

Tandem: Open the Space

Open the space of the active repository.

Tandem: Switch Repository

Change the repository Tandem works on.

Tandem: Activate Repository

Enable a repository that has no card yet.

Tandem: Show Defects

Render the defect ledger as a table.

Tandem: Open the Docs

Open this documentation.

The Projects view also carries New Product, New here…, Set Product…, Mark Done / Reopen and Choose Repositories to Read… on its items.

Settings

Setting Default Meaning

thinkubeTandem.storeRoot

empty

Root of the store. Empty means ~/thinkube-tandem-store; spaces persist at <root>/spaces/<project id>.

thinkubeTandem.groundingModel

opus

The model that works a thing out: its promises, the files they land in and the lines that must become true.

thinkubeTandem.volumeModel

sonnet

The model for the reading, the grouping, the naming of things, the questions and their answers, and the reading of the repository.

thinkubeTandem.workerModel

sonnet

The model the run’s workers use; never taken from the environment.

thinkubeTandem.workerModelByRole

{}

A different model for one kind of worker, for example {"judge": "opus"} for the one that decides whether a check is green.

thinkubeTandem.maxConcurrent

4

How many workers run at the same time.

thinkubeTandem.suiteCommand

npm test

The project’s own test suite. The closing gate runs it, and its verdict is on the report.

thinkubeTandem.prepareCommand

(machine-derived)

The build step a single check needs before it can run, such as compiling test files. The machine reads it from the repository’s own manifests; set it only to override what it read.

thinkubeTandem.docsGateMode

blocking

What Accept it does when the page a documentation promise named did not land: blocking refuses, advisory accepts and says so. Signing always needs the documentation promise or Not needed; this setting changes nothing there.

thinkubeTandem.giteaToken

empty

API token for a Gitea forge (github.com remotes use the gh CLI instead); Thinkube Git is a Gitea forge.

thinkubeTandem.controlUrl

empty

thinkube-control’s base URL, for the template catalogue and for making a new application. Empty reads it from the connected MCP server’s configuration.

thinkubeTandem.controlToken

empty

API token for thinkube-control. Empty reads it from the connected MCP server’s configuration.
